newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private stations say public TV expanding.
newsitem.headline: German private stations say public TV expanding.

text.p: The balance between public and private broadcasters in Germany is tipping increasingly in favour of the public stations, the association of private German broadcasters said on Tuesday.

A steady rise in political approval for special-interest programming licences and plans for digital broadcasting were giving public stations an advantage, the Association of Private Broadcasting and Telecommunications (VPRT) said in a statement.
The association also cautioned that private broadcasters were likely to take legal action to protect their interests and market share in the face of public expansion.
"That all German political parties have blatantly supported this position shows...that the dual broadcasting system is increasingly slanted to the detriment of private broadcasters," the VPRT said.

"It should therefore not be shocking if private broadcasters in the future bring suits before the European Commission in Brussels, or German courts, to protect their strength and development," it added.

The association cited a recent decision by public broadcaster ZDF television to move away from its joint morning programming with fellow public station ARD as evidence of the expansion in the state-funded sector.
